clarity.justification: The plan directly tests the hypothesis through one-language polarity probes, cross-language direction similarity, typology-error regression, activation patching, and steering, with directional predictions such as “negative-concord/double-negation languages incur excess double-negation/scope errors” and interventions that should “flip polarity” and “measure error reduction.” Refutation is conceivable and even acknowledged—“negation is largely language-specific, or typology has no effect”—but no numeric cutoff defines “largely shared,” “compact,” or a successful causal repair, so some conclusions require judgment. There is also a concrete specification inconsistency: the proposal says “10 languages” but lists eleven (five single-negation, four negative-concord, and French plus Portuguese), while the “double-negation-permitting/other” category leaves the relevant construction somewhat ambiguous.

feasibility.justification: The hardest step is the proposed repair that will “steer along the shared negation direction to enforce a single logical negation”; this requires custom choices about intervention sign, magnitude, and token position, but it is an implementable activation-steering operation supported by standard forward-hook and interpretability tooling rather than a magic step. The named artifacts—“Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Aya-23-8B, Gemma-2-9B”—exist, while linear probes, PCA/CCA, activation patching, layer sweeps, and regression all have mature implementations; the new multilingual stimulus set is explicitly constructed rather than assumed to exist. Resources are usefully quantified as “~800 minimal affirmative/negated sentence pairs,” four named model scales, and ten intended languages, although per-language item allocation and the exact amount of validation are unstated. The negative branch is runnable because the design includes chance and in-language probe comparisons, an “English-embedded control,” held-out constructions, non-negation tasks, single-negation-language specificity checks, and fluency filters, allowing absent transfer, absent typology effects, or nonspecific steering to be observed.
